conversations.content: The student framed the add-on round as one code submission covering both performance and Agent Prompt evaluation.
I discovered the upstream 2026-competition-round2 branch was a placeholder and that the repository already contained an earlier MiniVectorDB implementation with a MySQL 4.1 pipe protocol.

I retained the existing MySQL wire protocol because the task calls for a MySQL test driver over stdin/stdout, then replaced the snapshot-only engine with a CRC-framed WAL engine to remove repeated full-file rewrites.
I implemented exact L2 TopK with filtered candidate sets, primary-key tie breaking, transaction snapshots for rollback, and committed-frame recovery after a forced process stop.
conversations.evidence: minivectordb/engine.py methods _execute_sql, _select, begin, commit, rollback, and WAL replay.

conversations.content: The student requested an executable answer and supplied the final task constraints; the student did not claim independent authorship of the agent-written engine code.

implementation.protocol: MySQL 4.1 packet protocol over stdin/stdout; optional text mode for local debugging
implementation.storage: One CRC32-protected append-only frame per committed statement or explicit transaction in /data/wal.mvd, fsynced before success
implementation.transactions: BEGIN deep-copies the in-memory catalog; COMMIT appends buffered statements as one frame; ROLLBACK restores the copy and writes nothing
implementation.query: Exact L2 TopK with WHERE filtering before TopK; primary key ascending resolves distance ties
implementation.index: CREATE VECTOR INDEX is persisted as metadata; exact scans remain correct for both exact and ann requests

experiments.purpose: Verify SQL subset, filtered TopK, transactions, rollback, update/commit and reload.
Verify complete-frame and torn-tail recovery behavior.
experiments.details: Uncommitted data was absent after reopening; committed data survived; a deliberately truncated WAL tail was ignored without losing the preceding commit.

experiments.purpose: Verify the MySQL 4.1 handshake, authentication response, COM_QUERY, result set and EOF framing over stdin/stdout.
Verify compatibility with the locally installed MySQL 8 client through a test-only TCP relay.
experiments.command: python tests/test_mysql_client.py (test-only local TCP relay; requires mysql client)
experiments.observed_output: mysql_rc 0; stdout: 1\t0 and 2\t1.414213538; stderr empty; server stderr: minivectordb: ready (MySQL client version 8.0.46).

experiments.purpose: Measure the local 10K x 128 workload through the engine after replacing full-snapshot commits with WAL frames.
experiments.workload: 10,000 records, 128 dimensions, 100 insert batches of 100, 1,000 TopK=10 queries, half with category equality filter
experiments.observed_output: four local runs: totals 7.469 s, 7.605 s, 7.624 s, and 7.738 s; latest split insert 2.522 s, query 5.216 s
experiments.caveat: This is a local smoke benchmark, not an official rank or official cgroup/I/O measurement.

experiments.observed_output: Not run: Docker was unavailable on the local Windows host.
experiments.limitation: The Dockerfile and Linux x86_64 image need a final Linux build and smoke run.

iteration_history.observation: The earlier engine used a full JSON snapshot rewrite for every committed batch.
iteration_history.local_measurement: 10K insert phase took about 50.6 seconds during the version comparison.
iteration_history.change: Committed statements are now stored as CRC-framed WAL entries and replayed on startup.
iteration_history.result: The new engine's local insert phase measured 2.378 seconds.

iteration_history.observation: The vector matrix was initially rebuilt for every query in the implementation review.
iteration_history.change: The matrix cache is reused while the table version/alive-row set is unchanged and invalidated on mutation.
iteration_history.result: The revised engine completed the same local benchmark in 7.469-7.738 seconds across four runs.

student_evidence: The student supplied the task requirements and explicitly requested truthful, non-secret prompt evidence (u3-u6).
The student asked for the implementation plan and authorized completion (u5, u7).
No claim is made that the agent-written SQL parser, WAL format, or MySQL wire implementation was independently authored by the student.
retrospective: The task is a standalone database implementation, not a change to the seekdb kernel; separating parser, execution, persistence and wire transport made failures diagnosable.
Exact TopK is the safest correctness path when the public ANN parameter package is unavailable; it preserves Recall while the cache controls repeated matrix construction cost.
Filtering before ranking is a correctness invariant and is explicit in the execution path.
WAL frame atomicity is preferable to rewriting the entire data file for every 100-row ingestion batch under the stated I/O weighting.
The main remaining integration risk is the exact public driver framing and hidden cases; the official package was not present locally.
limitations: No external MySQL server or MySQL password is used.
The official hidden SQL cases and official performance baseline were unavailable locally.
Docker and the Linux x86_64 image were not built on the Windows development host.
ANN-specific index structures are not implemented; exact scans are used for both exact and ann requests.
Student-authored technical analysis is limited to the recorded prompts; agent decisions are explicitly labeled.
